title: VPC Shadow Deploy & Operator Firebreak Playbook — Safe Traffic Mirroring and Isolation
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook describes the procedure, configuration patterns, and operator guardrails for performing VPC shadow deployments and activating an "operator firebreak" (rapid traffic isolation) during mirrored-testing phases for Redwood Private deployments. Shadow deploys (traffic mirroring to a non-serving replica) let us validate model versions, runtime configs, and integration behavior under production traffic without impacting live responses. The operator firebreak is a controlled, automated isolation mechanism for quickly cutting mirrored test traffic and associated side-effects when abnormal signals are detected.

When to use this playbook

- Testing model variants (quantized, fp16, INT8) against real traffic before routing production traffic.
- Validating new batching/kv-cache config at scale.
- Verifying telemetry/observability changes (sampling, labels) under load.
- As a safety layer during cross-region control-plane handoffs where mirrored traffic could reveal regressions.

Owner and stakeholders

- Runbook owner: eng-private-deployments (oncall rotation: private-deploy-ops)
- Primary engineer: Aisha Patel (runtime-inference)
- Observability lead: Marcus Nguyen (eng-platform)
- Security reviewer: Lena Hoffmann (security-and-compliance)
- Customer success contact for field activations: Diego Alvarez

Prerequisites and constraints

1) Target environment: VPC-mode private deploys with mirrored egress allowed.
2) Control plane connectivity: control-plane-to-runtime channel must be up with TLS certs rotated in the last 90 days.
3) Traffic mirroring capability: either Envoy-based mirror filters (recommended) or SmartIngress version >= 3.4 that supports sampling-based mirroring.
4) Observability hooks: request_id propagation, sample trace capture, tokenized cost meter enabled.
5) Resource isolation: mirrored worker pool must run on labeled nodes with no write-back permissions to customer data stores (read-only KV access where required).

Minimum HW and network requirements

| Component | Minimum (single-zone test) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Shadow GPU pool | 2 x A100-40GB or equivalent | Separate node pool; no shared persistent volumes with prod pool |
| Control plane link | 100 Mbps dedicated path | Preferably private peering with <50ms RTT |
| Egress mirror bandwidth | 200 Mbps | Depends on request size; account for peak amplification from mirrored responses |
| Observability retention | 72 hours for shadow traces | Keep sampling higher for mirrored traffic |

High-level flow

1. Create a shadow model endpoint (read-only) with identical runtime version as candidate, but in "mirror" mode.
2. Configure network-level mirroring (Envoy or SmartIngress) to replicate 1–5% of production traffic (start at 0.1% for first trials).
3. Route mirrored traffic to the shadow pool on a dedicated tenant namespace with restrictive RBAC.
4. Ingest mirrored telemetry into a separate observability pipeline (tagged as "shadow=<id>").
5. Run automated regression checks and quality-evals against mirrored outputs.
6. Monitor guardrail signals; if any threshold fires, trigger operator firebreak.

Detailed operator steps

Preparation (T minus 72h)
1. Notify stakeholders (email and #private-deploy-ops slack) with planned windows and risk classification.
2. Ensure customer and legal approvals for mirrored traffic are documented for regulated customers.
3. Provision the shadow GPU pool; verify images are signed (SHA256) and attested.
4. Create a dedicated observability index (shadow-YYYYMMDD) and pre-provision retention.

Configuration (T minus 1h)
1. Deploy shadow endpoint YAML (example):

apiVersion: v1
kind: ShadowEndpoint
metadata:
  name: shadow-model-candidate-2028-02
  labels:
    shadow-run: "2028-02-03-aisha"
spec:
  model: candidate-v2-quant-int8
  runtimeImage: registry.redwood.ai/runtime:2028-01-14
  mode: mirror
  maxConcurrency: 8
  allowedWrites: none

2. Configure Envoy mirror filter on the prod route: (example snippet)

filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.router
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.config.filter.http.router.v2.Router
    start_child_span: true
    mirror_policy:
      filter:
        runtime_fraction:
          default_value:
            numerator: 1
            denominator: HUNDRED
      cluster: shadow-cluster

3. Validate RBAC: shadow namespace should have service accounts with read-only access to KV and no access to PII stores.

Smoke validation (T plus 0–10m)
1. Verify mirrored traffic arrives:
   - kubectl -n shadow logs deploy/shadow-proxy | grep "mirror.accepted"
2. Validate request count:
   - curl -sS "${OBS_API}/metrics?tag=shadow_run:2028-02-03-aisha" | jq '.requests'
3. Ensure mirrored responses are marked and not forwarded to downstream sinks: check proxy logs and dataflow "destination: shadow-sink (noop)"

Quality and safety checks (continuous)

Define these signals and thresholds. If any fire, the operator firebreak must be triggered immediately.

- Latency amplification: shadow p95 > prod p95 * 2.0 for 5 consecutive minutes -> FIREBREAK
- Error rate: shadow 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute increase compared to prod -> FIREBREAK
- Cost anomaly: token cost per request in shadow > prod by 3x for 10min -> REVIEW then FIREBREAK if sustained
- Privacy leak detection: any mirrored request containing PII that wouldn't be expected -> IMMEDIATE FIREBREAK and security pager
- Resource saturation: shadow GPU memory pressure > 80% for 3 minutes -> FIREBREAK

Operator firebreak activation (runbook)
1. Triage: Confirm alerts and correlate with smoke/test logs. 
   - Owner: oncall private-deploy-ops
2. Run automated containment (first-line): execute control-plane toggle to stop mirroring for the route.
   - CLI example: 
     redwoodctl mirror set --route product-api-v1 --percent 0 --reason "firebreak: <signal>"
3. If CLI is unavailable, apply Envoy patch to remove mirror cluster from route: 
   - kubectl -n prod patch envoyconfig product-api -p '{"spec":{"routes":[{"name":"/v1","mirror_policy":null}]}}' --type=merge
4. Verify containment: ensure shadow cluster receives no new requests.
   - kubectl -n shadow get hpa,deploy && kubectl -n shadow top pods
5. Notify stakeholders with incident stub (include alert IDs, chosen containment action, and next steps).

Post-firebreak analysis and remediation
1. Preserve evidence: export 72 hours of shadow traces and logs to the forensics index with access controls.
2. Root-cause analysis (RCA) timeline: 48 hours to produce a preliminary RCA; 10 business days for final RCA.
3. Rollback or forward decision matrix:
   - If signal is runtime config (batching/kv): revert to previous runtime config and re-run shadow with 0.1% traffic.
   - If model quality issue: roll model back in shadow and trigger regression eval on a copy of mirrored traces.
   - If network/control-plane bug: apply network fixes and validate with synthetic replay.
4. If the firebreak was triggered by privacy detection, follow Security breach playbook and notify legal immediately.

Roll-forward plan (if shadow run is healthy)

1. Increase mirror fraction in controlled steps: 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% with 30–60m observation windows between steps.
2. At each step run the automated quality-eval suite; require green on: latency SLOs, deterministic tokenization checks, and non-regression on top-100 prompt set.
3. After sustained green at 5% for 6 hours, schedule a canary routing test (real responses for a small subset) following the standard canary runbook.

Observability and dashboards

- Tagging: all mirrored requests must carry header X-Redwood-Shadow: <run-id>.
- Dashboards: shadow summary panel, latency amplification, error delta, token-cost delta, privacy flag counts.
- Alerting rules (examples):
  - alert: ShadowLatencyAmplification
    expr: (shadow_p95 / prod_p95) > 2 and increase_over_5m > 0
    for: 5m
  - alert: ShadowErrorRateIncrease
    expr: (shadow_5xx_rate - prod_5xx_rate) > 0.005
    for: 3m

Safety and compliance notes

- Data protection: mirrored requests may contain sensitive data. Shadow endpoints must never write to persistent customer stores. All shadow logs must be redacted according to the data-classification mapping and stored in a restricted index.
- Legal: obtain per-customer opt-in for mirrored traffic when required by contract and jurisdiction.
- Auditing: every mirror toggle (on/off/percent change) must be recorded in audit-log with user, timestamp, and rationale.

Operator checklists (quick reference)

Pre-start checklist:
- [ ] Stakeholders notified and approvals secured
- [ ] Shadow nodes provisioned and image attested
- [ ] Observability index created and access controlled
- [ ] RBAC verified for shadow namespace
- [ ] Mirror routing configured with initial fraction

Emergency break checklist:
- [ ] Confirm alert(s) and scope
- [ ] Execute mirror disable (redwoodctl or Envoy patch)
- [ ] Verify no shadow traffic in-cluster
- [ ] Preserve logs/traces and label evidence
- [ ] Open RCA ticket and assign owner

Appendices

A. Example redwoodctl commands
- Set mirror fraction:
  redwoodctl mirror set --route product-api-v1 --percent 1 --run-id 2028-02-03-aisha
- Disable mirror:
  redwoodctl mirror set --route product-api-v1 --percent 0 --reason "firebreak: latency-amplification"

B. Shadow endpoint teardown (safely decommission)
1. Scale shadow deployment to zero: kubectl -n shadow scale deploy/shadow-model --replicas=0
2. Remove mirror config and wait for 5 min to ensure no inflight mirrored requests.
3. Delete shadow namespace after log export: kubectl delete namespace shadow-2028-02-03-aisha

C. Short glossary
- Shadow deploy: non-serving replica that receives mirrored but non-responded traffic for validation only.
- Operator firebreak: human + automated action to stop mirrored traffic and isolate side-effects.
- Mirror fraction: percent of production requests duplicated to shadow.

Contacts and escalation

- oncall private-deploy-ops: +1-555-0101 (pager)
- Engineering pager: eng-pager@redwood.ai
- Security pager: sec-pager@redwood.ai

End of playbook
